editorial:
Imagine you are terrified for your life and the only person you can trust is the ex-boyfriend you probably shouldn't be calling. That is the mess Charlotte finds herself in. She is a young singer who ends up in a scary situation after her current partner is killed in his own home. She runs to Mathieu for help, but there is a huge catch: he is already living with his new girlfriend, Christine. You get this really tense vibe as these three people are stuck in one house, dealing with old feelings and new secrets. It feels like a pressure cooker where any one of them could snap at any moment.

What really works here is the acting, as you can feel the awkwardness and fear in every scene. The movie doesn't rush, which lets the tension build up slowly. While some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a huge action movie, the emotional drama is top notch. If you love stories about complicated relationships and mystery, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, the tension peaks when it is revealed that Charlotte was not as innocent as she claimed. The mystery of the murder is solved, showing that her fear was partly a cover for her own mistakes. Mathieu and Christine realize they cannot let her stay, and the three of them part ways. Charlotte finally faces the legal consequences of her actions, leaving the couple to rebuild their lives without her chaos.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological dramas and complicated love triangles.
